content:
You need a place where your church can meet and a clear reason for choosing it. Compare the same requirements at every venue, using the owner's terms and what you observe on site.

Use this guide to build a comparison sheet, check costs and discuss the tradeoffs. A score helps organize that discussion. It does not grant permission to use a building or replace checking the rental agreement.

---

## Define what the venue must do

Write your requirements before rating buildings. Separate conditions you must meet from preferences you can trade off. Keep a venue out of the final ranking while an essential condition remains unresolved.

Ask each owner whether your proposed worship use is permitted, which rooms you may use and which dates and access times they can offer. Describe your expected attendance and the time you need before and after the gathering.

School requests can involve priorities beyond your own calendar. Conway School District in Washington gives school and youth activities priority and reviews whether suitable space is available. Treat its process as a local example, then ask your prospective owner how approval works there.

<Callout type="warning">
Keep approval separate from scoring. Mark a missing permission or unanswered requirement as unresolved. Do not turn it into an average rating that disappears inside a total.
</Callout>

---

## Compare the surrounding areas fairly

Attach the area research from your demographic brief to each venue. Record the geography, table, period and margin of error with every American Community Survey estimate you use.

Use the same survey product and period across the areas you compare. Census guidance says to compare one-year estimates with one-year estimates and five-year estimates with five-year estimates. Check that the definitions and geographic boundaries match your question.

For small areas such as census tracts, the Census Bureau identifies five-year estimates as a source. These combine data collected across the period. Keep that period visible rather than labeling the figures as a current snapshot.

Use the findings to describe the surrounding area. Keep your observations about the building in a separate part of the sheet.

---

## Walk the site with access in mind

Use the Washington Governor's Office of the Education Ombuds event checklist as a starting point for a visit. It asks about accessible parking, entrances, meeting rooms, restrooms, seating and emergency exits. Involve people with disabilities in planning, as the checklist recommends.

- [ ] Follow the route from accessible parking or drop-off to the entrance.
- [ ] Check the routes to gathering rooms and restrooms.
- [ ] Identify barriers, unclear signs and inaccessible entrances.
- [ ] Check access to the speaking area and seating arrangements.
- [ ] Ask about emergency evacuation arrangements and assistance.

Record what needs follow-up with the owner. Keep these observations alongside the checklist rather than treating a general description of the property as proof that every room works for your gathering.

---

## Ask for the terms for your actual use

Request the agreement, fee schedule and insurance requirements for the rooms and activities you propose. At Conway, an approved applicant must provide proof of insurance, and the district arranges specific services with the applicant.

Theatres also need a specific inquiry. Regal's request form includes a Theatre Church option for weekly worship services. It asks about the planned start date and expected launch attendance. Use that route to ask about your proposed gathering instead of assuming a movie screening offer covers it.

Ask how competing uses affect the dates offered. Ask which staff and services come with access, and what happens when either party needs to change a reservation. Keep the owner's answers with the proposed agreement.

<Callout type="important">
Rental processes and examples were checked October 15, 2026. Confirm current availability, charges, deposits and insurance requirements directly with the named school district or theatre operator before committing funds.
</Callout>

---

## Compare the full cost of using the space

Build a cost sheet from each owner's written quote. Clover Park School District in Washington distinguishes space rental from special equipment and lighting. Its guidance also describes staffing charges, possible security and possible cleaning or damage deposits.

Use those categories as questions for every quote, not as charges you assume every venue imposes.

| Cost question | What to request |
|---|---|
| Space | Rooms included and chargeable hours |
| Staffing | Required staff and how their time is billed |
| Equipment | Included items and separately charged services |
| Cleaning and damage | Deposit terms and cleaning responsibilities |
| Insurance | Required evidence and coverage terms |

Ask whether billed time includes access before and after the gathering. Confirm staffing minimums and special-day charges in the owner's current schedule. Leave an unquoted item marked unresolved until you receive an answer.

---

## Build a simple scoring sheet

ASQ's decision-matrix procedure starts with criteria and relative weights. Give more weight to what matters most in this decision, then rate every eligible venue against the same criteria.

Use its simple scale of 1 for low, 2 for medium and 3 for high. Define what those ratings mean for each row before scoring. Higher must always mean more desirable, so label a cost row "affordability" rather than "cost."

| Criterion | Evidence beside the rating |
|---|---|
| Fit with intended area | Area brief and location notes |
| Usable gathering space | Rooms offered and site observations |
| Ease of access | Visit checklist and unresolved barriers |
| Affordability | Complete quote and required services |
| Practical access times | Owner's offered schedule |

Choose your own weights. Multiply each rating by its weight, then add the results for each venue. Retain the evidence beside the scores.

<Callout type="tip">
Write the rating definitions before comparing totals. A high affordability rating should mean a more affordable option, not a higher bill.
</Callout>

---

## Challenge the result

Discuss disagreements about ratings before settling on a total. ASQ advises reaching agreement rather than averaging conflicting ratings or taking a popularity vote.

Recalculate with different reasonable assumptions where your team disagrees. HM Treasury's decision-analysis guidance uses sensitivity analysis to examine how changes in scores or weights affect rankings. Apply that question here without presenting this simple worksheet as its formal appraisal method.

If a different assumption changes your preferred venue, record the tradeoff and investigate the disputed evidence. Do not change weights merely to make a favorite building win.

---

## Keep the reasons with the recommendation

Save the comparison, quotes, visit notes and unresolved questions together. Record which option you recommend and the evidence and assumptions behind that recommendation.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"He who responds with a word before he hears, It is folly and shame to him."* — Proverbs 18:13 (LSB)
</Callout>

Before committing, return to unresolved permissions and rental terms. The highest score is a prompt for discussion, not an instruction to sign.
excerpt: Compare venue permissions, access, rental costs and area data. Build a scoring sheet that keeps evidence and unresolved questions beside the ratings.
title: Comparing and Scoring Venues

sources.claim: Opening and section 1: compare consistent requirements; screening essential conditions before ranking is a practical adaptation, with unresolved as an editorial label.
sources.quote: Using the filter, any red-rated option choices will by definition fail to meet the minimum threshold for performance so would be dismissed from further consideration.

sources.claim: Opening, sections 1 and 4: obtain the owner approval, appropriate space and services; a worksheet is not rental permission.
sources.quote:
Application is reviewed by the district
Priority is given to school and youth activities prior to other groups
We check to see if we have an available space that fits the needs of the request

sources.claim: Sections 1, 4 and matrix: ask for proposed use, rooms, dates, access times, before/after gathering needs and expected attendance. Questions are a venue-comparison adaptation of owner inquiry fields.
sources.quote:
Planned Start/Launch Date
Expected Attendance at Launch
Event Access Start Time
I will require time after the event

sources.claim: Section 2: retain estimate uncertainty, geography, period and source details; distinguish observations as an editorial recordkeeping application.
sources.quote: To help you interpret the reliability of the estimates, the Census Bureau publishes a margin of error (MOE) for every ACS estimate.

sources.claim: Section 2: use consistent products, definitions and geographies when comparing areas.
sources.quote: Only compare 1-year estimates with 1-year estimates, and 5-year estimates with 5-year estimates.

sources.claim: Section 2: check comparability of variables and boundaries.
sources.quote: Because ACS variables and geographies may change over time, comparisons should be made with caution, or not compared at all.

sources.claim: Section 2: five-year estimates combine data across their period and cover tracts.
sources.quote:
60 months of collected data
Examining tracts and other smaller geographies because 1-year estimates are not available

sources.claim: Section 3: site visit checklist, parking, entrance and barriers; record observations and follow-up is an editorial application of checklist questions.
sources.publisher: Washington State Governor's Office of the Education Ombuds
sources.quote:
Is there accessible parking available and visible signage to find it?
Is this parking near an accessible entrance?

sources.claim: Section 3: entrances, routes to gathering rooms and restrooms, stage, seating and emergency exits.
sources.publisher: Washington State Governor's Office of the Education Ombuds
sources.quote:
Are meeting rooms along an accessible route of travel?
Is the stage or elevated speaking area wheelchair accessible?
Are emergency exits clearly identified and accessible?

sources.claim: Section 3: restroom route and seating questions.
sources.publisher: Washington State Governor's Office of the Education Ombuds
sources.quote:
Are restrooms along an accessible route of travel and next to or near training rooms?
Do not separate accessible seating from the group

sources.claim: Section 3: involve people with disabilities and ask about emergency evacuation assistance.
sources.publisher: Washington State Governor's Office of the Education Ombuds
sources.quote:
Involve people with disabilities in planning the event
Ensure that there are emergency procedures in place to address the evacuation and assistance of people with disabilities

sources.claim: Section 4: agreement and fee schedule are listed by owner; at Conway, an approved applicant must provide proof of insurance, and the district arranges specific services with the applicant. These are local requirements, not national rules.
sources.quote:
If approved, the applicant must provide proof of insurance
Arrangements are made with the applicant for specific services as needed
Facility User Agreement
Facility Rental Fees

sources.claim: Section 4: theatre church inquiries concern weekly worship; no claim that movie screening terms cover worship.
sources.quote:
Theatre Church
As the theatre church experts, Regal provides full-service consultation for churches looking to plant or expand their congregation by holding weekly worship services at the theatre.

sources.claim: Sections 4, 5, closing: ask about reservation changes and retain actual terms. Conway gives school/youth priority; questions about either-party changes do not assert a cancellation right.
sources.quote: Priority is given to school and youth activities prior to other groups

sources.claim: Section 5 and table: separate space cost from equipment/lighting and ask what is included.
sources.quote: All space rentals including auditoriums, gyms, performing arts centers (PAC), etc. are for the space only. Rentals do not include special equipment, lighting, etc.

sources.claim: Section 5: required staff, possible security and possible deposit; all are local examples, not national requirements or quoted prices.
sources.quote:
A CPSD staff member is required on-site for all facility use reservations. Current hourly rates will be applied.
Security may be required due to the size and/or nature of the event.
A cleaning and/or damage deposit may be required before an event.

sources.claim: Section 5: ask owner about billed access time, staffing minimums and special-day rates, without quoting their amounts or imposing them elsewhere.
sources.quote:
There is a 2-hour minimum staffing fee for weekend or holiday events. Includes ½ hour prior and ½ hour break down after event.
Double time rates are applied on holidays & District closure dates.

sources.claim: Section 6: relative weights, consistent ratings, arithmetic and evidence; criteria table adapts venue-owner and visit evidence to ASQ, not a new church-planting methodology.
sources.quote:
Assign a relative weight to each criterion, based on how important that criterion is to the situation.
Multiply each option’s rating by the weight. Add the points for each option.

sources.claim: Section 6: exact low/medium/high scale; high must favor selection; affordability row and tip adapt ASQ low-cost wording.
sources.quote:
1, 2, 3 (1 = low, 2 = medium, 3 = high)
Say "low cost" instead of "cost"; "ease" instead of "difficulty."

sources.claim: Section 6: retain evidence alongside ratings.
sources.quote: While a decision matrix can be used to compare opinions, it is better used to summarize data that have been collected about the various criteria when possible.

sources.claim: Section 7: resolve differing ratings rather than average or vote.
sources.quote: If individuals on the team assign different ratings to the same criterion, discuss until the team arrives at a consensus. Do not average the ratings or vote for the most popular one.

sources.claim: Section 7: test reasonable scoring/weighting disagreements and record changed rankings; warning against favoring a preferred building is an editorial application of testing assumptions.
sources.quote: The final step of the main MCDA process involves a sensitivity analysis to understand how the ordering of the options examined may change under different scoring or weighting assumptions.

sources.claim: Sections 7 and 8: simple worksheet is not formal Treasury appraisal; keep evidence and assumptions with the recommendation.
sources.quote:
MCDA should not be confused with simple scoring and weighting
By including the findings from the MCDA exercise in the final business case, analysts would then have a transparent record of the evidence and assumptions used to derive the shortlist

sources.claim: Opening and section 8: highest score informs discussion and does not mandate choice or signing.
sources.quote: The option with the highest score will not necessarily be the one to choose, but the relative scores can generate meaningful discussion and lead the team toward consensus

sources.claim: Section 8: exact Proverbs 18:13 LSB verse, opened individually on the publisher reader.
sources.publisher: The Lockman Foundation / Three Sixteen Publishing
sources.quote: He who responds with a word before he hears, It is folly and shame to him.

claim_check.notes: Independent Opus review passed 2026-10-15 at bd7f3d946a30b3d64ba6cebdc838e7683cefe9dc. The 635503e review checked all 25 sources, Proverbs 18:13 (LSB) and the screenshots, and failed only the Conway insurance sentence. bd7f3d9 changes only that sentence and source 11's claim. The new sentence says an approved applicant must provide proof of insurance; the live Conway page lists 'Application is approve or denied' and then 'If approved, the applicant must provide proof of insurance'. Lint passes (1,092 words, no warnings); desktop and mobile screenshots show all sections, tables, checklist, callouts and the LSB notice.

rulings: Scoring worksheet: Use an optional practical comparison sheet with team-chosen weights, ASQ low/medium/high scale and separate unresolved permissions. No mandatory weights or church-planting thresholds. This is simple scoring, not formal Treasury MCDA.
Venue examples: Use named Washington school owners and the directly opened Regal event inquiry form. Omit AMC and Regal marketing claims because their pages could not be opened.
